summary: The article provides a largely accurate and well-explained overview of the AICPI-IW and its impact on DA/DR for Central Government employees and pensioners.

claims.claim: The All-India Consumer Price Index for Industrial Workers (AICPI-IW) is a crucial economic indicator published by the Labour Bureau.
claims.note: The Labour Bureau, an attached office of the Ministry of Labour & Employment, Government of India, compiles and releases the AICPI-IW monthly.

claims.claim: The index is expressed with a base year, currently 2016=100, meaning all price changes are measured against the average prices in that base year.
claims.note: The new series of Consumer Price Index for Industrial Workers (CPI-IW) on base 2016 =100 has been effective from September 2020.

claims.claim: The Dearness Allowance for Central Government employees and pensioners is revised twice a year, effective from January 1st and July 1st.
claims.note: DA is revised twice a year, in January and July, based on the Consumer Price Index (changes in inflation and cost of living).

claims.claim: The percentage of DA is calculated based on the 12-month average of the AICPI-IW. While the exact formula can be complex, it generally involves a specific calculation using the average AICPI-IW numbers for a defined period (e.g., the last 12 months) relative to the base period used for the 7th Pay Commission recommendations.
claims.note: The government calculates DA using the 12-month average of the Consumer Price Index for Industrial Workers (CPI-IW). The formula was recommended by the 7th Central Pay Commission and has been followed since 2016.

claims.claim: Yes, Dearness Allowance (DA) is fully taxable as part of your salary income under the Income Tax Act, 1961. It is included in your gross salary for tax calculation purposes.
claims.note: DA is fully taxable under the Income Tax Act, 1961. Employees are required to declare it separately when filing Income Tax Returns.

claims.claim: Dearness Relief (DR) is the equivalent of Dearness Allowance (DA) but is paid to Central Government pensioners. Its purpose and calculation methodology, based on AICPI-IW, are identical to DA, aiming to offset inflation's impact on their pensions.
claims.note: Dearness Relief (DR) is a cost-of-living adjustment paid to government pensioners and family pensioners in India. It is introduced to protect pension income from inflation by increasing the pension amount whenever prices of essential goods and services rise.

article_title: 7th Pay Commission DA Hike: Understanding AICPI-IW's Impact
